description: How the claude CLI's stdout bytes become lines (HK-052). Each chunk is appended to a buffer and every complete line it finishes comes out, split on the byte 0x0A only: a carriage return stays part of its line, and empty lines are dropped. The bytes after the last newline wait for the next chunk, and come out only when the stream ends (the flush); a flush with nothing buffered gives nothing, and a flush empties the buffer, so a second one gives nothing either. A tail that grows past 16 MiB without a newline is dropped (HK-053), which a unit test proves rather than a case.
function: IOChannel.ingestStdout(_:) / flushStdoutRemainder() ↔ powerup_core::harness::claude::lines::LineBuffer — input {chunks: [line input], flush: bool}; expected {lines: [[string]] (the lines each chunk finishes, one list per chunk), remainder: string|null (what the flush gives; null when there is no flush or nothing buffered)}

cases.name: a partial line waits for more data
cases.reason: Splitting per chunk would hand half a JSON object to the parser; the tail waits (HK-052).

cases.name: a carriage return stays in its line
cases.reason: Only 0x0A splits; the parser accepts the trailing \r as JSON whitespace (HK-052).

cases.name: a lone carriage return does not split
cases.reason: A CR alone is not a line break (HK-052).

cases.name: a line of a carriage return alone is kept
cases.reason: Only a line with no bytes at all is dropped (HK-052).

cases.name: several lines in one chunk
cases.reason: One read can carry many lines; they come out in order (HK-052).

cases.name: one line split over three chunks
cases.reason: A line comes out only when its newline arrives (HK-052).

cases.name: a character split between chunks is joined
cases.reason: Splitting is on bytes, so a multi-byte character cut by the pipe is whole again in its line (HK-052).

cases.name: the flush gives the unterminated tail
cases.reason: A last line without a newline is still read when the process exits (HK-052).

cases.name: without a flush the tail stays buffered
cases.reason: Nothing comes out of the buffer until the stream ends (HK-052).

cases.name: a flush with nothing buffered gives nothing
cases.reason: An empty stream has no remainder (HK-052).

cases.name: a flush after a complete line gives nothing
cases.reason: A newline-terminated stream leaves nothing behind (HK-052).

cases.name: an empty chunk gives nothing
cases.reason: A zero-length read finishes no line (HK-052).
